saints.name: St. Maximilian
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A young North African who refused conscription into the Roman army for conscience's sake and was executed for the name of Christ…
biography: At Theveste in Numidia, the modern Tébessa of Algeria, on 12 March 295, Maximilian, son of the Christian veteran Fabius Victor, was brought before the proconsul Dion to be enrolled in the Roman army, for he had reached the age of twenty-one and owed the state his service.

"I cannot serve," he answered; "I am a Christian." When Dion offered the military seal, he refused it, saying he already bore the seal of Christ, and neither threats nor his father's presence moved him. Condemned, he was beheaded the same day; his father returned home, the Acts relate, giving thanks to God.

The "Acta Maximiliani," composed within a few years of his death and reckoned among the most authentic records of the early martyrs, preserve the dialogue of his trial. As the first Christian known to have died for refusing military service, he is invoked as the patron of conscientious objectors, and his name is kept on 12 March in the Roman Martyrology.
saints.knownFor: His witness of conscience recorded in the “Acta Maximiliani.”
